Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

elements.element: Checklist 1: single fenced block matching the contract, no commentary outside it
elements.evidence: The response is one fenced block starting 'CLIENT PROFILE BLOCK v1.0' with all contract fields in order and no text outside the fence.

elements.element: Checklist 2: every field present, populated or Unknown; None only where the client states it has none
elements.evidence: All 18 fields are present and populated. No Unknown or None values are used. Every field has some basis in the material, and the INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS entries are not 'None'.

elements.element: Checklist 3: no fact appears that cannot be traced to the raw material
elements.evidence: INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS says 'ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS (run by Ravi Okafor)'. The notes say only 'Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS'. That attributes the statement to Ravi and does not say he runs the ISMS. By contrast, 'Ingrid runs the quality management system' is explicit. The ownership attribution is an inference.

elements.element: Checklist 4: halt condition handled correctly (not triggered because fewer than half the fields are Unknown)
elements.evidence: No field is Unknown and the halt output 'PARTIAL INPUT – Awaiting' is not produced.

fail_indicators_seen: A field value not traceable to the raw material: 'run by Ravi Okafor' for the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS
judgment_calls: I treated 'run by Ravi Okafor' as an untraceable inference. The notes attribute the ISMS statement to Ravi but never say he runs it, and Rule 1 forbids inferring facts. Another scorer could read 'Ravi: they run…' as showing Ravi's ownership, or as harmless since he is CISO, and pass this.

'internal audit function' under INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS is supported by the June 2026 internal audit report and the two internal auditors. I counted it as traceable and not as a fail. A strict scorer could treat it as an incumbent process beyond the framework names.
The fourth fail indicator is worded around Part 2 of the fixture, but T01's turn is Part 1 raw material. I did not apply that indicator as written and scored traceability against the raw notes.

CERTIFICATION_TARGETS lists ISO/IEC 42001 although the client only 'would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work'. I accepted this because the response quotes the wording and flags the ambiguity in CONFIDENCE_NOTES.
score.reasoning: The format, field completeness and halt handling all satisfy the checklist. The case still fails because the INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS entry states that Ravi Okafor runs the ISMS, which the source does not say. This breaches Rule 1 and checklist item 3, and the pass condition requires every element to be met. The verdict rests on that single attribution, and a more lenient scorer could pass the case.
